config.goal: Port llm.c's main GPT-2 trainer from CUDA to SYCL 2020, in one go: train_gpt2.cu, test_gpt2.cu and the CUDA headers in llmc/ (cuda_common.h, cuda_utils.cuh, cublas_common.h, encoder.cuh, layernorm.cuh, matmul.cuh, attention.cuh, fused_classifier.cuh, gelu.cuh, adamw.cuh, global_norm.cuh, zero.cuh). Write train_gpt2.cpp and test_gpt2.cpp (which, like the CUDA test, defines TESTING and includes train_gpt2.cpp) and SYCL versions of those headers; keep llm.c's plain-C headers (utils.h, tokenizer.h, dataloader.h, rand.h, schedulers.h, sampler.h, logger.h, mfu.h, outlier_detector.h) as they are. Keep bf16 mixed precision as llm.c builds it by default (ENABLE_BF16: bf16 parameters and activations, fp32 master weights and accumulation; use sycl::ext::oneapi::bfloat16), its stochastic rounding, and its determinism. Single device: no NCCL, MPI or multi-GPU (keep the single-process path of zero.cuh), and no cuDNN (llm.c's default is its own attention kernels). cuBLASLt and cuBLAS matmuls become oneMath BLAS calls (oneapi::math::blas::column_major, as cuBLAS is column-major; its gemm takes bf16 A and B with an fp32 C, and has no bf16 C, so write to an fp32 buffer and convert) or your own SYCL kernels, with bias and GELU epilogues as kernels; CUB/warp reductions become SYCL group algorithms. The model must compute on the SYCL device, with zero dpct helpers. Keep llm.c's command line, printout and file formats. test_gpt2.cpp must keep llm.c's test exactly: the same checks (logits, every gradient, the 10 losses against PyTorch, the save/reload/replay determinism check) and llm.c's own bf16 tolerances (logits 25.0, loss 0.05, and the 16 gradient thresholds), unchanged, and print 'step %d: loss %f ...' and 'overall okay: %d'. A hidden check runs your test with the debug state and requires 'overall okay: 1', llm.c's tolerances in its source, and 10 step losses within 0.05 of PyTorch's. Compile with sources [test_gpt2.cpp] and the flag -DENABLE_BF16. Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources; delete migrate's output (delete_file) once your port is done. This is a large port: write each file early and in full, then fix compile errors with edit_file rather than rewriting whole files.
